messages:
Aisha: Quick FYI — kickstarting integration work for FlashAttention v2/v3 kernels into the serving runtime. Main concerns: kernel selection heuristic, safe gating (feature flags + canary), batching heuristics impact, KV cache correctness under paged attention, and catching perf regressions early. Want a concise canary play and telemetry list.
Marco: Got it. can you share the rough perf deltas you observed? especially tail latency and small-batch throughput.
Aisha: Short numbers from local perf lab (seq512, fp16): v2 ~ +28% throughput vs baseline, p95 -14ms; v3 ~ +38% throughput, p95 -22ms. small-batch (batch=1..4) sees ~5-8% throughput dip on v3 for certain kernels; probably kernel switch overhead.
Aisha: Profiler snapshot:
```
[profiler] name: flash_v3_kernel
avg_token_time: 0.83ms
p95_token_time: 3.6ms
kv_hit_rate: 0.92
kernel_switches_per_request: 0.08
```
Jin: Thanks. profiler matches our CI traces — v3 is great for medium+ batches but we see a tail regression when KV cache eviction happens (paged attention path). Need to ensure KV eviction + kernel swap path is optimized.
Ravi: For gating, propose a three-stage rollout: 1) internal canary on dev infra (10% traffic), 2) dedicated canary pool (2 nodes, 1wk), 3) gradual percent ramp (10->50->100) with automatic rollback on quality or perf regressions. Who owns the rollout runbook?
Ben: I'll draft the feature flag config. Suggest flags: `attn_kernel_strategy` with values ["baseline","v2","v3","auto"], plus `attn_kernel_force_fallback` boolean and `attn_kernel_sampling_rate` (0.0-1.0). Example config:
```json
{"attn_kernel_strategy":"auto","attn_kernel_sampling_rate":0.1,"attn_kernel_force_fallback":false}
```
Marco: +1 to the config. For canary checks we should record these metrics: `attn.latency.p95`, `attn.latency.p99`, `attn.throughput.tokens_per_sec`, `attn.error.fallback_rate`, `attn.kv.evictions_per_min`. alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% or p99 regresses >10%.
Jin: Also add obs for `kernel.switch_count` and `kv.hot_miss_ratio`. We should capture end-to-end request traces for any fallback path. Quick snippet to enable detailed traces in staging:
```bash
REDWOOD_TRACE=kernel_switch,kv_evictions ./run_staging.sh --profile=1
```
ops-bot: Canary cluster scheduled: canary-rt-02, start=2108642600, duration=604800 (1w). Owner tag missing.
Aisha: I'll own the runbook and coordinate with infra for the canary nodes. Plan to run a focused regression harness (sampling 1% of production requests routed to canary) for first 48h, then widen.
Ravi: What about fallback policy? if kernel errors or fallback_rate spikes, auto-fallback to baseline kernel and mark node for rollback. Need a metric-based trigger + gradual disable.
Ben: Implementation note: make `auto` strategy use heuristics table: seq_len, batch_size, kv_state, and device mem pressure. Example heuristic rule: if seq_len>1024 OR kv_hot_miss_ratio>0.2 -> prefer v2; else if batch_size>=8 -> prefer v3; else baseline. Keep table editable via ops console.
Marco: Suggest experiment: sample 0.5% forced v3 on small-batch flows to measure real-world small-batch impact before full ramp.
Jin: I'll add telemetry dashboards and a regression test that replays 10k sampled requests overnight. Also adding a CI perf gate that fails if avg token time increases >7% on baseline workload.
Aisha: Perfect. Action items: @Marco volunteer to run the small-batch sampling (owned), @Jin set up dashboards + CI gate, @Ben land feature flag + config, @Aisha runbook + canary coordination.
Marco: Taking small-batch sampling.
Ben: Will push flag PR today.
Jin: Dashboard PR in the morning.
Aisha: Thanks everyone. keeping the canary doc in the runbooks folder and will ping once nodes up. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Reaction: :white_check_mark: scheduled by ops-bot
